timecoded_text_to_speech.text: One of the perks of working in laser psychiatry is that we come across patients with cases that are not really, really common, that conditions like NMD and Catholicists, patients with, again, like delusionary parasythosis, patients with morbid jealousy.
And these are the patients, they are very delusional, very high risk to themselves, high risk to others.
And it's always, as I mentioned in the beginning, it's a mystery where you just unfold each and every individual case and provide treatment until they're according to the need of the patient.

I'm an only lecturer in the School of Medicine at the University of Liverpool and I've been involved in the teaching of undergraduate and postgraduate medical students and I regularly sit as an examiner for the undergraduate medical students.
I have a particular interest in research and personality disorder and also in the management of psychiatric, secretly, of neurological conditions.
I've done my master's in research and personality disorder and I have published several papers in Machozenfield.
I know the work culture, I know how things operate in Mercycare.

There are now many, many more leadership and management rules for the trainees and for the new consultants and the trust encourages them to develop special interests and to contribute towards the successful growth of the trust.

So what I felt that this trust offers is the excellent training under the supervision of excellent consultants with experience in wide range of specialities, ranging from forensic to early intervention to eating disorder, liaison psychiatry.
And I guess this is something that Mercycare has the edge over other trusts where the trust offers so many other subspecialities of psychiatry training.
